User Story: As a registered customer, I want to log in with my username and password, so that I can access my account.
Given: a registered user with valid credentials
Then: the system returns 200 with an access token, a refresh token, the user ID and the username

User Story: As a registered customer, I want to log in with my username and password, so that I can access my account.
Given: a registered user who enters an incorrect password
Then: the system returns 400 with the message "Invalid Credentials" and does not return a token

User Story: As a logged-in customer, I want to view my profile details, so that I can confirm my account information is correct.
Given: a logged-in user with a valid access token
Then: the system returns 200 with their details, including ID, username, email, first name and last name

User Story: As a logged-in customer, I want to view my profile details, so that I can confirm my account information is correct.
Given: a request with no access token
Then: the system returns 401 with the message "Access Token Is Required"

User Story: As a logged-in customer, I want to view my profile details, so that I can confirm my account information is correct.
Given: a request with an invalid or expired access token
Then: the system returns 401 with the message "Invalid/Expired Token"

User Story: As a customer, I want to browse the list of available products, so that I can find something to buy.
Given: a customer browsing the catalog (no login required)
Then: the system returns 200 with a list of products and the total, skip and limit values

User Story: As a customer, I want to browse the list of available products, so that I can find something to buy.
When: the customer supplies limit and skip values
Then: the system returns only the requested number of products, starting from the requested position
Notes: Test the limit and skip query parameters in Postman

User Story: As a customer, I want to browse the list of available products, so that I can find something to buy.
Notes: Proposed target to be agreed with the business; the single run in TC-03 took 2,900 ms

User Story: As a customer, I want to view the details of a single product, so that I can decide whether to buy it.
Then: the system returns 200 with the product's ID, title, price, category and stock

User Story: As a customer, I want to view the details of a single product, so that I can decide whether to buy it.
Given: a product ID that does not exist
Then: the system returns 404 with a message stating that the product with that ID was not found

User Story: As a store admin, I want to add a new product to the catalog, so that customers can see and buy it.
Given: an admin who supplies a title and a price
Then: the system returns 201 with the new product's ID, title and price

User Story: As a store admin, I want to add a new product to the catalog, so that customers can see and buy it.
Given: an admin who submits the add-product request with an empty body
Then: the system rejects it with 400 and a message that names the missing required fields
Notes: 400 is a BA assumption; re-run TC-12 as POST /products/add with body {}

User Story: As a store admin, I want to add a new product to the catalog, so that customers can see and buy it.
When: the admin requests it using the returned ID
Notes: Call GET on the returned ID after the add

User Story: As a store admin, I want to update an existing product's details, so that the catalog stays accurate.
Given: an existing product ID and a changed field (for example the title)
When: the admin submits the update request
Then: the system returns 200 with the updated values

User Story: As a store admin, I want to update an existing product's details, so that the catalog stays accurate.
Then: the system returns the updated values
Notes: Call GET on the same ID after the update

User Story: As a store admin, I want to delete a product that is no longer sold, so that customers do not see it.
When: the admin submits the delete request
Then: the system returns 200 with the deleted product's data

User Story: As a store admin, I want to delete a product that is no longer sold, so that customers do not see it.
Notes: Call GET on the same ID after the delete

User Story: As a store owner, I want adding, updating and deleting products to be limited to authorized admins, so that customers cannot change the catalog.
Given: a request to add, update or delete a product with no valid access token
Notes: All three calls succeeded with no token (Auth Needed? = No)

User Story: As a store owner, I want adding, updating and deleting products to be limited to authorized admins, so that customers cannot change the catalog.
Given: a logged-in user who does not have admin rights
When: they attempt to add, update or delete a product
Notes: Needs a defined role model; not tested
